jobs.description:
**Summary**
-----------


This position is the lead physical scientist for hydrology \& geomorphology on the TRRP Science Branch team. Involves managing technical studies, integrating results into program guidance, and providing scientific \& design input for restoration projects such as flow releases, bank work, gravel augmentation, riparian \& floodplain restoration, sediment management, and watershed improvements. Focuses on developing flow\-release hydrographs \& evaluating geomorphic, hydrologic, and thermal responses.


Learn more about this agency


  
**This job is open to**
-----------------------


### **The public**


U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.
### **Career transition (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL)**


Federal employees whose job, agency or department was eliminated and are eligible for priority over other applicants.
### **Clarification from the agency**


This announcement is open to U.S. Citizens or Nationals; and Career transition eligibles (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL).


  
**Duties**
----------


This position is located within the Department of the Interior, Bureau of Reclamation, Trinity River Restoration Division in Weaverville, California.  

  

In this role, you will apply advanced hydrologic principles and analytical methods to evaluate water resources, support park management decisions, and ensure compliance with federal policies. You will provide technical expertise, conduct field investigations, analyze data, and prepare scientific reports to guide resource protection and operational planning.  

  

Hydrologist (GS\-09/11/12\) \- Major Duties


* Collect and analyze water data using field instruments, computer models, and mapping software to support water resource projects and studies.
* Prepare technical reports and present findings to project teams, using clear visuals and summaries to inform decisions on water management.
* Coordinate with engineers, biologists, and other specialists to plan and carry out field investigations, ensuring accurate data collection and safe operations.
* Review and interpret regulations, policies, and scientific literature to recommend solutions for water quality, supply, and environmental compliance issues.
* Lead or contribute to project planning, budgeting, and progress tracking, using project management tools and collaborating with internal and external partners.

  

  

Progression by Grade \- duties will be developmental in nature when filled below the full performance level.


* At the GS\-09 (starting) level, perform tasks under close supervision, focusing on learning procedures and applying established methods.
* At the GS\-11 (developmental) level, work more independently, handle moderately complex assignments, and begin to provide technical guidance to others.
* At the GS\-12 (full performance) level, serve as a technical expert, lead projects, and make recommendations that influence program direction and resource allocation.


  

Physical Demands: The work is typically performed in an office setting with no special physical demands. However, work may also be performed in the field which involves periods of walking, bending, climbing, or driving motor vehicles to worksites. The work may also involve some overnight travel for training, meetings, and site visits.  

The work regularly combines both office and field assignments. Field work requires physical exertion, such as long periods of standing, or recurring and considerable walking, stooping, bending, crouching, crawling, and climbing such as in regular and periodic construction activities and field inspections. Work may also include frequent lifting of moderately heavy items weighing less than 50 pounds. Field assignments may also involve operating small watercraft, driving motor vehicles to work sites, some of which may be remote, and include overnight stays in remote locations.  

  

Work Environment: The work is usually performed in an office setting. However, work time may also be spent periodically visiting field sites. Field site visits are typically performed in either an outdoor setting subject to weather changes, diverse terrain, and safety hazards associated with working around complex features and/or construction, or an industrial setting subject to noise, fumes, and moving machinery. Both settings may require the use of personal protective equipment. Safety precautions and protocols are observed at all times and the scientist complies with safety instructions and regulations and ensures individual and others safety by promptly reporting unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and accidents to the supervisor.  

  

The work involves regular and recurring exposure to moderate risks, discomforts, and unpleasantness such ask high noise levels, infectious materials, or toxic or irritating chemicals; travel in safety approved small aircraft and watercraft; high winds and low or high temperatures; infestation of dangerous reptiles or poisonous plants, snakes, or insects; adverse weather conditions; noxious fumes; flammable liquids; or radiation. The work involves performing tasks in close proximity to rotating heavy mechanical and electrical machinery and may involve working within confined spaces for extensive periods of time. Special safety precautions such as protective clothing and gear are necessary. Safety precautions and protocols are observed at all times and the scientist complies with safety instructions and regulations and ensures individual and others safety by promptly reporting unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, and accidents to the supervisor.

jobs.description:
**Position Description**
------------------------


**Check out what the team is up to, and what they have to offer!**


https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/cd418c7ce7d846618cf14d09da16ad50


The Program Coordinator reports to the FERC License Program Manager and provides program coordination and support for the FERC License Program. This position supports the successful delivery of major programs and projects associated with ongoing FERC license compliance, as well as upcoming FERC relicensing, surrender, and transfer activities for Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric projects.


This position supports compliance with requirements established by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), including the Division of Licensing and the Division of Hydropower Administration and Compliance (DHAC), as well as internal programmatic systems and processes. The Program Coordinator assists with tracking license implementation activities, interim and formal schedules, and program milestones to support timely and compliant execution of FERC license requirements. Major tasks include developing and maintaining schedules, budgets, tracking tools, program documentation, reporting, and internal and external communications as well as identification and escalation of issues, risks, and emerging concerns.


The position supports Tacoma Power’s mission to create clean, reliable, and marketable energy while ensuring responsible stewardship of natural and cultural resources. Program activities span a broad range of resource areas, including fish and wildlife, forestry, land management, recreation, cultural resources, instream flows, water quality, and reservoir management.


The Program Coordinator plays an integral role in supporting the FERC Licensing Program and ensuring the current and future goals and obligations associated with Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric project licenses are accomplished in a coordinated, timely, and compliant manner. The position works collaboratively across programs and disciplines within Tacoma Power to align FERC licensing and compliance activities with related operational, environmental, regulatory, and resource stewardship efforts.  

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Coordinate FERC Licensing Program activities** by serving as a member of the FERC Licensing Core Team and supporting coordination across relicensing, license surrender, transfer, and compliance efforts. Facilitate action\-item tracking, decision documentation, communications, and alignment of critical program activities.
* **Develop and maintain program controls and tracking systems** for FERC licensing and compliance activities, including scopes, schedules, budgets, critical paths, milestones, resource availability, risks, action items, and other program performance measures. Provide timely information and reporting to support program management and decision\-making.
* **Coordinate project teams and advisory groups** supporting Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric licenses by facilitating communication, accountability, and alignment among internal teams, consultants, contractors, agencies, and stakeholders. Identify emerging issues and support timely escalation and resolution of risks affecting program objectives.
* **Support FERC license compliance and regulatory requirements** for Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric projects by monitoring license obligations, reporting requirements, payments, FERC exhibits, agency and stakeholder commitments, and other compliance activities. Track license requirements and deadlines to support timely completion and reduce regulatory risk.
* **Coordinate meetings, communications, and program materials** for senior management, internal and external teams, advisory groups, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders. Develop agendas, presentations, briefing materials, action\-item records, and decision documentation to support effective program communication and governance.
* **Support contracts, task orders, submittals, and program documentation** associated with FERC licensing, relicensing, surrender, transfer, and compliance activities. Coordinate with internal records and information management resources to maintain accurate, accessible, and appropriately controlled program documentation and ensure required FERC submittals are completed and filed on schedule.
* **Promote continuous improvement and professional development** by identifying opportunities to improve program coordination, tracking, reporting, and information management processes; coordinating across related utility functions; and maintaining knowledge of FERC licensing and compliance practices through relevant training, conferences, and professional development.

jobs.description:
Research Faculty**Description**
---------------

 **University of Colorado Cancer Center; Colorado School of Public Health**

**Department: Population Health Shared Resource; Health Systems, Management, \& Policy**

**Job Title: Data Analyst, Senior Professional Research Assistant Level 3**

**Position \#:00853267 – Requisition \#: 41110**

**Job Summary:**

  

The University of Colorado Comprehensive Cancer Center (UCCC) is looking to hire a full\-time Senior Professional Research Assistant (Sr. PRA) – Level 3 within the Population Health Shared Resource (PHSR), a shared resources that provides quantitative and behavioral support to Cancer Center members and the university. The PHSR Data Analyst will be responsible for managing data and conducting analyses, meeting with investigators to determine the parameters of their projects and consulting with the PHSR Director(s) and Administrator to identify the best resources to meet user needs; maintaining appropriate records of work/service performed. PHSR maintains a large portfolio of cancer\-related projects, and the position offers the opportunity to grow as a researcher with strong mentorship and the resources provided by the university the Cancer Center.


This position is for a Core\-based Sr PRA 3– where Core members are usually expected to possess higher technical skills, educational training and interpersonal skills while operating a highly\-expensive, sophisticated, cutting\-edge equipment, and advanced data analysis supporting a wide variety of project and collaborating with multiple researchers’ campus\-wide.


Key Responsibilities:

* Provide scientifically rigorous database management and statistical analysis for multiple grant\-funded research projects
* Collaborate with Principal Investigators and other stakeholders to discuss project needs
* Creatively and effectively integrate data from multiple sources
* Check data for integrity
* Assist with the development of tables, reports, analysis as directed by project leaders
* Provide input into publications and interdepartmental projects
* Conduct analysis of SEER, SEER\-Medicare linked data, All\-Payers Claims Databases, MarketScan, electronic health records, and other sources of data
* Conduct analysis of cancer registry data
* Write methods and results drafts for manuscripts
* Maintain documentation of analyses
 **Work Location**

 **Why Join Us:**

  

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in\-person meetings.

  

PHSR is a campus\-wide shared resource, operated under the umbrella of the Cancer Center. It is Colorado’s only National Cancer Institute\-designated comprehensive cancer center, a distinction recognizing its outstanding contributions to research, clinical trials, prevention and cancer control. CU Cancer Center’s clinical care sites are UCHealth, University of Colorado Hospital and Children’s Hospital Colorado are ranked nationally by U.S. News and World Report. The CU Cancer Center’s vision is to “prevent and conquer cancer. Together.” We do this through our mission statement of “uniting our community to overcome cancer through innovation, discovery, prevention, early detection, multidisciplinary care and education.” The CU Cancer Center oversees and supports twelve advanced Shared Resources (from basic science cell technologies to omics to population health science), with the PHSR being one of them. Our expertise across cancer types helps us provide world\-class treatment for common cancers, while offering hope for many patients with difficult or aggressive tumors who have struggled to find treatment options elsewhere.

You will provide technical expertise, conduct field investigations, analyze data, and prepare scientific reports to guide resource protection and operational planning.  

  

Hydrologist (GS\-09/11/12\) \- Major Duties


* Collect and analyze water data using field instruments, computer models, and mapping software to support water resource projects and studies.
* Prepare technical reports and present findings to project teams, using clear visuals and summaries to inform decisions on water management.
* Coordinate with engineers, biologists, and other specialists to plan and carry out field investigations, ensuring accurate data collection and safe operations.
* Review and interpret regulations, policies, and scientific literature to recommend solutions for water quality, supply, and environmental compliance issues.
* Lead or contribute to project planning, budgeting, and progress tracking, using project management tools and collaborating with internal and external partners.

  

  

Progression by Grade \- duties will be developmental in nature when filled below the full performance level.


* At the GS\-09 (starting) level, perform tasks under close supervision, focusing on learning procedures and applying established methods.
* At the GS\-11 (developmental) level, work more independently, handle moderately complex assignments, and begin to provide technical guidance to others.
* At the GS\-12 (full performance) level, serve as a technical expert, lead projects, and make recommendations that influence program direction and resource allocation.


  

Physical Demands: The work is typically performed in an office setting with no special physical demands. However, work may also be performed in the field which involves periods of walking, bending, climbing, or driving motor vehicles to worksites. The work may also involve some overnight travel for training, meetings, and site visits.  

The work regularly combines both office and field assignments. Field work requires physical exertion, such as long periods of standing, or recurring and considerable walking, stooping, bending, crouching, crawling, and climbing such as in regular and periodic construction activities and field inspections. Work may also include frequent lifting of moderately heavy items weighing less than 50 pounds. Field assignments may also involve operating small watercraft, driving motor vehicles to work sites, some of which may be remote, and include overnight stays in remote locations.  

  

Work Environment: The work is usually performed in an office setting. However, work time may also be spent periodically visiting field sites. Field site visits are typically performed in either an outdoor setting subject to weather changes, diverse terrain, and safety hazards associated with working around complex features and/or construction, or an industrial setting subject to noise, fumes, and moving machinery. The work involves regular and recurring exposure to moderate risks, discomforts, and unpleasantness such ask high noise levels, infectious materials, or toxic or irritating chemicals; travel in safety approved small aircraft and watercraft; high winds and low or high temperatures; infestation of dangerous reptiles or poisonous plants, snakes, or insects; adverse weather conditions; noxious fumes; flammable liquids; or radiation.
